en.greeting: Hi! You already know walked and watched. Today: the common verbs that don't take -ed, plus didn't and Did you…? Let's go step by step.

steps.title: Verbs with their own past
steps.text: Most verbs add -ed for the past. But the verbs we use most often have their own past form.
steps.body: Verbs that add -ed are **regular**: *walk → walked*. These ten are **irregular** (tidak beraturan): each has its **own past form**, and there's no rule. Learn them like new words, in pairs: *go–went, eat–ate*. Never add -ed to them (not 'goed', 'eated'). Indonesian never changes the verb (*kemarin saya pergi*), but English does: **Yesterday I went**, not 'Yesterday I go'. Say them out loud: **said** sounds like 'sed', and in **bought** the gh is silent ('bot').

steps.title: Last Sunday
steps.text: Here is Rina's family day out last Sunday. Spot the irregular verbs.
steps.body: The past form is the **same for every person**: *I got, we went, my son said*. No -ed, and no -s for he/she: *she went*, not 'she wents'. **take** is also for transport (*took a taxi* = naik taksi), and **have** is also for meals (*had dinner* = makan malam).

examples.en: On Sunday I got up at seven.
examples.id: Hari Minggu saya bangun jam tujuh.

examples.en: We went to Ragunan Zoo.
examples.id: Kami pergi ke Kebun Binatang Ragunan.

examples.en: We took a taxi from our house.
examples.id: Kami naik taksi dari rumah.

examples.en: The children saw the elephants.
examples.id: Anak-anak melihat gajah.

examples.en: My husband bought es kelapa for everyone.
examples.id: Suamiku membeli es kelapa untuk semua orang.

examples.en: We had dinner at my mother's house and came home at nine.
examples.id: Kami makan malam di rumah ibuku dan pulang jam sembilan.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Bu Ani is back from her holiday. Which verb fits?

question.prompt: Complete: Bu Ani ___ a lot of photos in Bali last month.
question.explanation: **last month** is the past, and **take** is irregular: its past is **took**. 'taked' adds -ed to an irregular verb, and 'takes' is the present.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Rina cooked for her friends last night.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Rina membuatkan nasi goreng untuk kami.
question.solution: Rina made fried rice for us.
question.explanation: **make** is irregular: the past is **made** (not 'maked'). The order is who + verb + what + for whom: **Rina made fried rice for us.** Notice *fried rice*: the describing word comes first (nasi goreng → fried rice).

steps.title: Saying no: didn't + base verb
steps.text: To say something didn't happen, English uses one helper word: didn't.
steps.body: **didn't** (= did not) + the **base verb** (kata kerja dasar, the dictionary form: *go, eat, see*): *I went* → **I didn't go**. Why not 'didn't went'? **did** is the past of *do*, so **did already shows the past**; the main verb goes back to its base. You know this from *She doesn't work* (does takes the -s). The same works for regular verbs: *didn't watch*, not 'didn't watched'. Don't just add *not* like Indonesian *tidak pergi*: 'I not went' is wrong.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Dimas was late for a concert on Saturday. What happened?

question.prompt: Which sentence means 'Dimas tidak membeli tiket'?
question.explanation: **didn't + base verb**: did already shows the past, so the verb goes back to **buy**. 'didn't bought' shows the past twice, and 'not bought' is missing **did**.

steps.title: Asking with Did
steps.text: Questions about the past use did too.
steps.body: Put **Did** before the **subject** (who you ask about), then the **base verb**: *She went home.* → **Did she go home?** Not 'Did she went' (did already shows the past). With a question word, it goes first: **What did you eat?** Indonesian asks with normal order (*Kamu makan apa?*), but English needs did. Short answers use did, not the main verb: **Yes, she did.** / **No, they didn't.** Don't mix in was/were: 'Were you go…?' is wrong.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: You want to ask a colleague about Sari's trip on Friday.

options: Did she took the train to Bandung?
Was she take the train to Bandung?
Did she take the train to Bandung?
question.explanation: **Did + subject + base verb**: **Did she take…?** 'Did she took' shows the past twice, and **was** can't go with another verb like *take*.

steps.title: Listen and answer
steps.text: Your friend Budi asks you something. Press play and listen.

question.listen: Did you get my message last night?
question.prompt: Listen to Budi's question. The answer is yes. Choose your short answer.
question.explanation: Budi asks **Did you get my message last night?** A **Did you…?** question is about you, so answer with **I** + **did**: **Yes, I did.** 'Yes, I was' answers a *Were you…?* question, and 'she' is someone else.

steps.title: Quick review
steps.text: Flip through these cards to lock in the past forms.

flashcards.back: He didn't eat the cake. (Dia tidak makan kuenya.)

flashcards.front: Short answer (no): Did Rina call you?

steps.text: Here's everything on one page. Keep it for later.

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · irregular past + did
artifact.intro: Twelve common verbs with their own past form, and how to make negatives and questions with did.
tips: The past form is the same for every person, with no -ed and no -s: **I went, she went, they went**.
Negative: **didn't + base verb**: **I didn't go** (not 'didn't went'). did already shows the past.
Question: **Did + subject + base verb**: **Did you see it?** Short answers: **Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.**

id.greeting: Hai! Kamu sudah tahu walked dan watched. Hari ini: kata kerja umum yang tidak memakai -ed, ditambah didn't dan Did you…? Ayo kita pelajari pelan-pelan.

steps.title: Kata kerja dengan bentuk lampau sendiri
steps.text: Kebanyakan kata kerja ditambah -ed untuk masa lalu. Tapi kata kerja yang paling sering dipakai punya bentuk lampau sendiri.
steps.body: Kata kerja yang ditambah -ed disebut **regular** (beraturan): *walk → walked*. Sepuluh kata ini **irregular** (tidak beraturan): masing-masing punya **bentuk lampau sendiri**, tanpa aturan. Hafalkan seperti kosakata baru, berpasangan: *go–went, eat–ate*. Jangan pernah ditambah -ed (bukan 'goed', 'eated'). Bahasa Indonesia tidak mengubah kata kerja (*kemarin saya pergi*), tapi bahasa Inggris mengubahnya: **Yesterday I went**, bukan 'Yesterday I go'. Ucapkan keras-keras: **said** dibaca 'sed', dan di **bought** huruf gh tidak dibaca ('bot').

steps.title: Minggu lalu
steps.text: Ini cerita jalan-jalan keluarga Rina hari Minggu lalu. Cari kata kerja tidak beraturannya.
steps.body: Bentuk lampaunya **sama untuk semua orang**: *I got, we went, my son said*. Tanpa -ed, dan tanpa -s untuk he/she: *she went*, bukan 'she wents'. **take** juga dipakai untuk kendaraan (*took a taxi* = naik taksi), dan **have** juga untuk makan (*had dinner* = makan malam).

examples.en: On Sunday I got up at seven.
examples.id: Hari Minggu saya bangun jam tujuh.

examples.en: We went to Ragunan Zoo.
examples.id: Kami pergi ke Kebun Binatang Ragunan.

examples.en: We took a taxi from our house.
examples.id: Kami naik taksi dari rumah.

examples.en: The children saw the elephants.
examples.id: Anak-anak melihat gajah.

examples.en: My husband bought es kelapa for everyone.
examples.id: Suamiku membeli es kelapa untuk semua orang.

examples.en: We had dinner at my mother's house and came home at nine.
examples.id: Kami makan malam di rumah ibuku dan pulang jam sembilan.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Bu Ani baru pulang liburan. Kata kerja mana yang cocok?

question.prompt: Lengkapi: Bu Ani ___ a lot of photos in Bali last month.
question.explanation: **last month** itu masa lalu, dan **take** tidak beraturan: bentuk lampaunya **took**. 'taked' menambah -ed pada kata kerja tidak beraturan, dan 'takes' itu bentuk sekarang.

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Tadi malam Rina memasak untuk teman-temannya.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Rina membuatkan nasi goreng untuk kami.
question.solution: Rina made fried rice for us.
question.explanation: **make** tidak beraturan: bentuk lampaunya **made** (bukan 'maked'). Urutannya siapa + kata kerja + apa + untuk siapa: **Rina made fried rice for us.** Perhatikan *fried rice*: kata sifatnya di depan (nasi goreng → fried rice).

steps.title: Kalimat negatif: didn't + kata kerja dasar
steps.text: Untuk bilang sesuatu tidak terjadi, bahasa Inggris memakai satu kata bantu: didn't.
steps.body: **didn't** (= did not) + **kata kerja dasar** (bentuk kamus: *go, eat, see*): *I went* → **I didn't go**. Kenapa bukan 'didn't went'? **did** adalah bentuk lampau dari *do*, jadi **did sudah menunjukkan masa lalu**; kata kerja utamanya kembali ke bentuk dasar. Kamu sudah tahu ini dari *She doesn't work* (does mengambil -s). Kata kerja beraturan juga sama: *didn't watch*, bukan 'didn't watched'. Jangan hanya menambah *not* seperti *tidak pergi*: 'I not went' itu salah.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Dimas terlambat datang ke konser hari Sabtu. Apa yang terjadi?

question.prompt: Kalimat mana yang artinya 'Dimas tidak membeli tiket'?
question.explanation: **didn't + kata kerja dasar**: did sudah menunjukkan masa lalu, jadi kata kerjanya kembali ke **buy**. 'didn't bought' menunjukkan masa lalu dua kali, dan 'not bought' tidak memakai **did**.

steps.title: Bertanya dengan Did
steps.text: Pertanyaan tentang masa lalu juga memakai did.
steps.body: Taruh **Did** di depan **subjek** (siapa yang kamu tanyakan), lalu **kata kerja dasar**: *She went home.* → **Did she go home?** Bukan 'Did she went' (did sudah menunjukkan masa lalu). Kalau ada kata tanya, kata tanyanya di depan: **What did you eat?** Bahasa Indonesia bertanya dengan urutan biasa (*Kamu makan apa?*), tapi bahasa Inggris perlu did. Jawaban singkat memakai did, bukan kata kerja utamanya: **Yes, she did.** / **No, they didn't.** Jangan dicampur dengan was/were: 'Were you go…?' itu salah.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Kamu ingin bertanya ke rekan kerja tentang perjalanan Sari hari Jumat.

options: Did she took the train to Bandung?
Was she take the train to Bandung?
Did she take the train to Bandung?
question.explanation: **Did + subjek + kata kerja dasar**: **Did she take…?** 'Did she took' menunjukkan masa lalu dua kali, dan **was** tidak bisa dipakai bersama kata kerja lain seperti *take*.

steps.title: Dengar dan jawab
steps.text: Temanmu Budi menanyakan sesuatu. Tekan play dan dengarkan.

question.listen: Did you get my message last night?
question.prompt: Dengarkan pertanyaan Budi. Jawabannya ya. Pilih jawaban singkatmu.
question.explanation: Budi bertanya **Did you get my message last night?** Pertanyaan **Did you…?** itu tentang kamu, jadi jawab dengan **I** + **did**: **Yes, I did.** 'Yes, I was' menjawab pertanyaan *Were you…?*, dan 'she' itu orang lain.

steps.title: Ulangan singkat
steps.text: Balik kartu-kartu ini supaya bentuk lampaunya makin melekat.
